report:
# Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?

**Verdict:** 📚 Published evidence only

## What the research and analysis found

The published evidence does not show that cracking your knuckles causes arthritis. [s0c146902-effect, s17e3d0b7-effect] Multiple studies, including systematic reviews and X-ray studies, found no link between habitual knuckle-cracking and osteoarthritis or arthritis in the hands. [s0c146902-effect, s18a7ea9d-effect, s0f057a10-effect, s57056354-effect] Some studies did find that habitual knuckle crackers were more likely to have hand swelling or weaker grip, but these were not arthritis. [sc0fcfcda-effect, s7628770e-effect, s134aee18-effect] Because the best available evidence is observational, certainty is low.

## Question (PECO)

- **Population:** adults who crack their knuckles regularly
- **Exposure:** repeatedly bending and flexing the fingers to produce a popping sound in the joints
- **Comparator:** not cracking knuckles
- **Outcome:** diagnosed osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis in hand joints, based on clinical examination or imaging
- **Time window:** over the lifetime
- **Estimand:** ATE, risk difference, deviations handled n/a

## Causal graph (DAG)

- knuckle_cracking → arthritis: the question being tested
- age → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- age → knuckle_cracking: assumed (no source)
- sex → arthritis: assumed (no source)
- family_history_oa → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- prior_joint_trauma → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- heavy_manual_labor → arthritis: cites s3956555d-design
- knuckle_cracking → hand_swelling: cites sc0fcfcda-effect, s7628770e-effect, s134aee18-effect, saf6268ba-effect
- knuckle_cracking → grip_strength: cites sc0fcfcda-effect, s7628770e-effect, s134aee18-effect, saf6268ba-effect
- hand_swelling → arthritis: assumed (no source)
- grip_strength → arthritis: assumed (no source)

Treated as exogenous (the model's judgment that nothing in the graph can cause it; no source): age, sex, family_history_oa, prior_joint_trauma, heavy_manual_labor.

## Key confounders

- age

## Evidence

**Certainty:** low (starts low: best evidence is observational)

Evidence flow: 74 sources found → 51 studies after dedupe → 38 included (excluded: off_topic 10, not_a_study 2, wrong_outcome 1).

- [Systematic Review Knuckle Cracking Arthritis](https://www.instagram.com/popular/systematic-review-knuckle-cracking-arthritis) — systematic_review, year unknown, known only from secondary sources: no link between habitual knuckle-cracking and arthritis
- [Let's get a hand on this: Review of the clinical anatomy of "knuckle cracking".](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30080300) — systematic_review, 2018: failed to show an association
- [No, habitual knuckle popping, or cracking (over the course of several decades) isn’t associated with clinical or radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis](https://cdn.mdedge.com/files/s3fs-public/JFP06510725.PDF) — cross_sectional, year unknown, known only from secondary sources: no significant association between crack years and OA (distal interphalangeal joint, mean 108 crack years; metacarpal phalangeal joint, mean 75 crack years)
- [Effects of habitual knuckle cracking on metacarpal cartilage thickness and grip strength.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2468122916301049) — cross_sectional, 2017: habitual KC appears to be associated with increased MH cartilage thickness
- [Study on the effects of cracking your knuckles](https://www.goldenstateortho.com/about/news-events/news/does-cracking-knuckles-cause-arthritis-no) — cross_sectional, 2015, known only from secondary sources: knuckle crackers did not show any hand problems from the practice.
- [Knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis.](https://www.jabfm.org/content/24/2/169) — cross_sectional, 2011: prevalence of any KC among the controls (23.2%; n = 19) was not significantly different from prevalence in persons with OA (18.0%; n = 24; P = .361)
- ["Knuckle Cracking": Can Blinded Observers Detect Changes with Physical Examination and Sonography?](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5339152) — cohort, 2017: a small increase in ROM among joints that cracked compared with those that did not
- [Knuckle cracking: secondary hyperparathyroidism and what your mother did not tell you.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4438371) — case_control, 2013: no objective difference in the incidence of arthritis between the groups
- [A 2011 study went further by removing the guesswork of self-diagnosis. Researchers reviewed hand X-rays from 215 adults aged 50 to 89 and compared radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis against each person’s knuckle-cracking history.](https://acibademinternational.com/blog/is-it-bad-to-crack-your-knuckles-the-60-year-experiment-that-answered-it) — cross_sectional, 2011, known only from secondary sources: no association between knuckle-cracking history and radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis
- [Effect of habitual knuckle cracking on hand function.](https://europepmc.org/article/med/2344210) — cross_sectional, 1990: habitual knuckle crackers were more likely to have hand swelling and lower grip strength
- [Does knuckle cracking lead to hand osteoarthritis?](https://highperformancept.nyc/library_newsfeed_125) — cross_sectional, 2011, known only from secondary sources: prevalence of KC among the controls was 23%, which was not significantly different from the prevalence in those with OA, which was 18%
- [No Association Between Knuckle Cracking and Osteoarthritis: A Cross-Sectional Study of 300 Adults Aged 45 and Older](https://acibademinternational.com/blog/does-cracking-your-knuckles-cause-arthritis) — cross_sectional, 1990, known only from secondary sources: the rate of osteoarthritis was no higher in the crackers than in everyone else
- [Real-time visualization of joint cavitation.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4398549) — cross_sectional, 2015: joint cracking is the result of cavity inception within synovial fluid rather than collapse of a pre-existing bubble
- [A 2011 study published in the Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine looked at 215 people between ages 50 and 89 who had had an X-ray of their right hand during the previous five years.](https://creakyjoints.org/living-with-arthritis/cracking-knuckles-cause-arthritis) — cross_sectional, 2011, known only from secondary sources: The researchers found a similar incidence of knuckle OA in any one joint among people who said they cracked their knuckles and those who didn’t, irrespective of how frequently or for how many years the person cracked.
- [Clinical Inquiry: Does knuckle popping lead to arthritis?](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27846331) — cross_sectional, 2016: Habitual knuckle popping, or cracking (over the course of several decades) isn't associated with clinical or radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis.
- [Does knuckle cracking lead to arthritis of the fingers?](https://www.mcgill.ca/oss/article/medical-you-asked/cracking-your-knuckles-not-bad-it-sounds) — case_control, 1998, known only from secondary sources: The prevalence of arthritis in any joint was the same in subjects who crack their knuckles (18%) and those who don’t (21%)
- [A more recent retrospective study examined the history of knuckle cracking in 215 osteoarthritis patients and compared them to controls without the condition](https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20260807-should-i-stop-cracking-my-knuckles) — case_control, 2017, known only from secondary sources: the amount and duration of knuckle cracking over someone's lifetime had no effect on their osteoarthritis risk
- [The consequences of habitual knuckle cracking.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1130029) — cross_sectional, 1975: effect not verified
- [Evaluation of Students Self-Joint Cracking Habits: A Cross-Sectional Study](https://www.mevlanamedsci.org/pdf/evaluation-of-students-self-joint-cracking-habits-a-cross-sectional-study) — cross_sectional, year unknown: effect not verified
